results.title: the runtime role is not superuser and does NOT have BYPASSRLS
results.detail: noramedi_app: super=false bypassrls=false · noramedi_platform: super=false bypassrls=false · noramedi_migrator: bypassrls=true

results.title: the runtime role owns NONE of the guarded tables
results.detail: all four owned by noramedi_migrator

results.title: all four guarded tables have RLS ENABLED and FORCED
results.detail: Clinic, Patient, PaymentPlan, PaymentPlanInstallment — all ENABLE + FORCE

results.title: no policy contains an IS NULL escape hatch
results.detail: 4 tenant policies, all with USING + WITH CHECK, none permissive on a missing setting

results.title: ENABLE only: the table OWNER bypasses a deny-all policy entirely
results.detail: owner sees 2/2 rows despite USING (false) — this is the trap FORCE exists to close

results.title: adding FORCE closes it: the same owner, same policy, now sees nothing
results.detail: owner sees 0/2 rows — the ONLY thing that changed is the FORCE flag

results.title: removing FORCE restores the bypass, confirming the flag is the cause
results.detail: bypass returns with NO FORCE and disappears with FORCE — reversible and attributable

results.title: a query with NO tenant context returns zero rows on every guarded table
results.detail: Patient 0 · PaymentPlan 0 · PaymentPlanInstallment 0 · Clinic 0 — fail closed, not fail open

results.title: an INSERT with NO tenant context is refused by WITH CHECK
results.detail: refused with P2010

results.title: an EMPTY context value is treated as missing, not as a wildcard
results.detail: empty string -> NULL -> no rows (nullif() in app_current_organization_id is what does this)

results.title: a MALFORMED context value returns zero rows
results.detail: zero rows. NOTE: NoraMedi ids are `text`, not `uuid`, so a malformed value cannot raise a cast error — it simply matches nothing. A uuid-typed column would fail LOUDER; see the evidence document.

results.title: a role with no policy at all on a FORCE'd table sees nothing (deny by default)
results.detail: RLS with no matching policy denies — a forgotten policy hides data rather than exposing it

results.title: tenant A sees its own patients and nothing else
results.detail: 2 rows, both organization A

results.title: a clinic-1-restricted context does NOT see clinic 2 of its own organization
results.detail: cross-clinic-within-one-organization is a DIFFERENT boundary from cross-organization, and it holds

results.title: the organization-scoped table returns only the caller’s organization
results.detail: 2 clinics, both organization A

results.title: a parent-scoped child is visible only through a parent the caller can read
results.detail: the EXISTS-through-parent policy resolves against a parent that is itself under RLS

results.title: legitimate same-tenant writes are NOT blocked (false-denial bar)
results.detail: insert + update + delete of the caller’s own row all succeed — a guard that fails closed too aggressively breaks the product

results.title: tenant A cannot READ tenant B’s patient by primary key
results.detail: 0 rows — an explicit primary-key lookup is still filtered by the policy

results.title: tenant A cannot UPDATE tenant B’s row (0 rows affected, not an error)
results.detail: 0 rows affected; verified unchanged via the BYPASSRLS migrator role

results.title: tenant A cannot DELETE tenant B’s row
results.detail: 0 rows affected; row still present

results.title: tenant A cannot INSERT a row carrying tenant B’s clinic
results.detail: refused with P2010

results.title: THE PAIRING ATTACK: A’s organizationId with B’s clinicId is refused by WITH CHECK
results.detail: refused with P2010

results.title: a tenant cannot MOVE its own row into another tenant
results.detail: refused with P2010

results.title: a bulk UPDATE spanning both tenants touches only the caller’s rows
results.detail: an UNQUALIFIED `UPDATE "Patient" SET ...` affected 2 rows, not 4 — the policy is the WHERE clause

results.title: a bulk DELETE spanning both tenants deletes only the caller’s rows
results.detail: 1 row deleted, tenant B untouched

results.title: tenant A cannot read tenant B’s clinic, payment plan or installment
results.detail: all three foreign lookups return 0

results.title: a row the caller CANNOT SEE is still a valid foreign-key target
results.detail: confirmed invisible — the next experiment inserts a row REFERENCING it anyway

results.title: RLS does NOT stop a cross-tenant FK reference when the policy does not mention it
results.detail: ROW WAS CREATED linking tenant A’s plan to tenant B’s patient. RLS is additive, not sufficient — the F3-2 Prisma guard refuses this same write (tenantGuardIsolation.test.ts §E).

results.title: a FK to a NON-EXISTENT row still fails normally (the gap is visibility, not integrity)
results.detail: refused with P2010 — referential integrity is intact; only VISIBILITY is bypassed

results.title: the context is visible for the whole interactive transaction
results.detail: stable across multiple statements and an intervening sleep

results.title: after COMMIT the setting is GONE — this is what makes transaction pooling safe
results.detail: setting is NULL and the query sees 0 rows — transaction-local, not session-local

results.title: after ROLLBACK the setting is gone too
results.detail: a failed transaction leaves no tenant residue on the connection

results.title: NEGATIVE CONTROL: a SESSION-scoped setting DOES leak past its transaction
results.detail: session-scoped value survived the commit, transaction-scoped value did not — the difference is is_local

results.title: tenant identity CANNOT be changed mid-transaction to escalate
results.detail: the policy re-evaluates per statement; the setting is application-issued, never client-supplied. This is why the Node-side context (F3-2) must remain the only writer.

results.title: 40 interleaved transactions over a 3-connection pool never cross tenants
results.detail: 40 transactions, 3 connections, 0 leaks

results.title: the platform role reaches every tenant through a POLICY, not through BYPASSRLS
results.detail: 4 rows across both organizations — granted by an explicit `TO noramedi_platform` policy on exactly the four tables, so break-glass is a reviewable grant rather than an unconditional override

results.title: the platform role is NOT omnipotent: a table with no platform policy stays closed
results.detail: break-glass is scoped to the tables its policies name — adding a table does not silently widen it
